asks: How is a held request refused on each kind of connection?
answer: By what the connection can carry. On a request to a model provider, Silo replies with the status 400 in the provider's own error format, with Silo's words as its message: every agent program tried stops on it within seconds and shows the words. Only the model request is refused, never the program's own sign-in or settings calls on the same host. On another request Silo reads, it replies with the status 403 and a body that says denied, or held and not answered. A push Silo reads is answered in Git's own terms: the status 200, Silo's words as `remote:` lines, and each branch rejected with the reason. On a TCP connection Silo does not read, it resets the connection. On a name lookup, it answers that the lookup is refused. On other UDP traffic, such as QUIC, which has no connection to reset, it answers that the port cannot be reached, so that the program stops waiting or falls back to TCP at once. When the program no longer listens, nothing is sent. In every case the record says how the hold ended. Each agent program's version is checked against these answers by the live check of `denial-per-program`.
